text:
marta.design: Pushed a proto for a compact onboarding stepper that appears as a floating mini-card in the corner and expands into a lightweight modal stepper. Intent: guide users through 3 small wins (create project, create API key, run sample). Need quick feedback on copy tone, step ordering, keyboard flow, and a11y.

lucas.product: Love the micro-journey. A couple product points: 1) Make samples optional but visible as a 'Try demo' step. 2) If a user already has projects, skip the first step and surface 'Open existing project' instead.

zhou.eng: Implementation notes: floating mini-card is easy; expand into modal uses existing dialog component. We'll hydrate personalization after initial paint. Persist user progress server-side for auth users; localStorage fallback for guests. Events planned: `onboard.stepper_shown`, `onboard.stepper_step_completed`, `onboard.stepper_dismissed`, `onboard.stepper_sample_launched`.

emma.a11y: Accessibility quick list: 
- Floating card must be in tab order and have descriptive label e.g., "Onboarding steps, collapsed" that toggles to "Onboarding steps, expanded" via `aria-expanded`.
- When modal opens, move focus to first actionable step; when closed, restore focus to toggle.
- Use `role=dialog` + `aria-modal=true` for the modal variant and set `aria-labelledby` to the stepper header.
- Each step action should have descriptive labels: avoid single-word CTAs like "Go" or "Try"; prefer "Create API key" / "Launch Chat demo (2m)".
- Announce progress changes through `aria-live` polite region: "Step 1 of 3 completed".
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for expand animations.

marta.design: Copy drafts: 
Variant 1 (friendly): Headline "Quick start in 3 steps" / Steps: "Create your first project" (Create project), "Create API key" (Create key), "Run a demo" (Launch Chat demo) / Microhint: "Get end-to-end running in ~3 minutes"
Variant 2 (goal-focused): Headline "Get to first result" / Steps: "Create project" / "Add API key" / "See sample response" / Microhint: "Hands-on in minutes"

lucas.product: Prefer Variant 1. Also add a small progress indicator (dots + text) and an optional skip link "Skip setup". For experiments, add query param `?stepper_variant=alpha` for 10% rollout.

zhou.eng: For skip/skipped state: store `userPrefs.onboarding_stepper_skipped=true`; if skipped, surface a subtle left-rail badge "Setup" so users can reopen. We'll debounce show for 24 hours for new orgs to avoid immediate nag.

emma.a11y: A couple more nits: 
1) If using images or thumbnails in steps, include `alt` and don't rely on them for meaning. 
2) Ensure color contrast for progress dots and microhint in dark mode; some mock colors are below 4.5:1 at 12px.

marta.design: OK will swap to darker microhint and adjust progress colors. Also I'll change CTAs to full descriptive text and add estimated time chips on sample steps.

lucas.product: Analytics we want: `onboard.stepper_seen`, `onboard.stepper_interaction`, `onboard.stepper_complete`, `onboard.stepper_reopen`. Tag events with `variant`, `org_id_present:true/false`, and `user_tenure_days`. We'll run for 2 weeks and measure time-to-first-success and sample-launch rate.

zhou.eng: I'll wire up the events. Small implementation detail: batch events client-side to save network calls during onboarding flows. Also will expose an API to mark a step as completed from server-side flows (e.g., project created via CLI).

emma.a11y: Test matrix request: keyboard-only, VoiceOver on mac, NVDA+Firefox, and high-contrast theme. Acceptance criteria: focus moves predictably, aria-live announcements fire, no keyboard traps, visible focus indicators in all themes.

marta.design: Action items: update prototype with Variant 1 copy, darker microhint, descriptive CTAs, ETA chips, and accessible labels. Add acceptance criteria and link to ticket.

preview-bot: Staging preview queued: https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/2100  smoke tests scheduled.

marta.design: Thanks all 44dI'll post updated mocks and the A11y checklist to the ticket later today."
